highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, the new flagship model featuring a 1M token context window and fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is now the default Opus model in Claude Code, making it significantly more capable for large codebases and long-running agent tasks. Developers should update their Claude Code installation to take advantage of the new model automatically.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.221: Focus View for VS Code
highlights.summary: VS Code users can now toggle a Focus View using Ctrl+Alt+F (or the 'Claude Code: Toggle Focus View' command) that hides noisy tool activity behind a collapsible per-turn summary with a live running-tool indicator. This is great for developers who find the tool call output distracting while Claude is working through complex tasks. The feature makes it much easier to track what Claude is doing at a glance without being overwhelmed by intermediate steps.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.222: Worktree Isolation Security Fix
highlights.summary: This security-focused release fixes a critical bug where worktree-isolated sessions and their subagents could run destructive git commands against the main checkout. Isolation now correctly applies to file edits and Bash commands across every session type, including background agents. It also fixes a bypass where PreToolUse auto-allow hooks could circumvent tool restrictions in background agent tasks — update immediately if you use worktrees or background agents.

highlights.title: Claude Code Full Course – Autonomous Goals, MCP, and VS Code Setup
highlights.summary: This comprehensive YouTube course covers setting up Claude Code in VS Code from scratch, including configuring MCP (Model Context Protocol) and working with autonomous agent goals. It is an excellent starting point for developers who want a structured, end-to-end introduction rather than piecing together documentation. Watch it if you are new to Claude Code and want to understand how all the major features fit together.

highlights.title: Agent-Manager: A Tmux TUI for Running Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
highlights.summary: Agent-Manager is an open-source terminal UI built on Tmux that lets you run and manage multiple AI coding agents — including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode — side by side in one interface. This is useful for developers who want to orchestrate several agents in parallel without juggling multiple terminal windows. Check out the GitHub repo to see if it fits your multi-agent workflow.

highlights.title: Agent Skills That Bring Team Coding Standards to Claude Code and Codex
highlights.summary: This open-source project lets teams define shared 'agent skills' — reusable instructions and coding standards that can be loaded into Claude Code or Codex to enforce consistent patterns across a whole team. It solves the common problem of every developer having different Claude prompts and conventions, leading to inconsistent AI-generated code. Great for engineering leads who want to standardize how their team uses AI coding assistants.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 Added as Default, Network Allowlist, and New Hook
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.219 adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model, introduces a `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting to block all non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting, and adds a `DirectoryAdded` hook for reacting when new directories appear in your workspace. The strict network allowlist is a powerful security improvement for teams running Claude Code in sandboxed CI/CD environments. Update and explore the new hook if you are building custom automation around Claude Code events.

tips_of_the_day: Use Ctrl+Alt+F in VS Code to toggle Claude Code's new Focus View — it collapses verbose tool output into a clean per-turn summary, so you can stay in flow while Claude works without losing visibility into what it's doing.

If your team uses Claude Code, create a shared CLAUDE.md or agent skills file (like the tikalk/adlc-team-skills pattern) that encodes your coding standards — this ensures every developer gets consistent, on-brand AI suggestions without manual prompt repetition.

When running Claude Code in CI or sandboxed environments, set `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` to explicitly whitelist only the hosts your agent needs — this prevents unexpected outbound calls and makes your pipeline audits much cleaner.
